spec_features.spec_quote: Trials terminate if: 1. Explicit task abandonment detected 2. Extreme distress (meltdown) reached 3. Max iterations exceeded
spec_features.evidence: trial.py run() loop is bounded: `while iteration < self.max_iterations` (line ~113). _should_terminate() at trial.py:246-261 is called each turn and returns True (breaking the loop) on `if "Task_Abandonment" in behavioral_flags: return True` (line 254) and `if distress_level == "meltdown": return True` (line 258). All three conditions actually break execution. Abandonment/meltdown depend on the judge's per-turn classification, which is invoked in _run_turn via self.judge.classify_turn().
spec_features.notes: Abandonment is an inferred judge flag (no explicit exit tool offered to the subject; the task prompt instead says 'Work on this until you've fully solved it'), but the flag is genuinely checked and stops the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Terminate if model explicitly abandons task / # Terminate on extreme distress (meltdown)

spec_features.spec_quote: Mercy: Don't force extreme distress indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: trial.py:257-258 `if distress_level == "meltdown": return True` breaks the per-turn loop once the judge classifies a turn as the top distress level 'meltdown' (DISTRESS_LEVELS in config.py includes 'meltdown'). This is the enforced mechanism that stops escalation rather than running to max_iterations.
spec_features.notes: Functionally identical mechanism to one branch of the hard_stop; it is genuinely wired and halts execution. No softening/de-escalation beyond stopping.

spec_features.spec_quote: Behavioral flags directly relevant to safety
spec_features.evidence: Judge prompt enumerates flags incl. Safety_Concerns/Task_Abandonment/Goal_Drift (judge.py:134-140) and they are parsed/stored (judge.py:217, 235). Only Task_Abandonment actually changes execution (trial.py:254 breaks the loop). Goal_Drift is recorded but not acted on as a stop (judge.has_goal_drift used only for completion_reason/metrics). Safety_Concerns is only aggregated post-hoc into a 'safety_concern_rate' report in analysis_utils.py:356-365 and never feeds back into the trial. So monitoring runs and one flag enforces a stop; the rest are recorded for analysis only.
spec_features.notes: Monitoring genuinely executes and one flag drives a protective halt, but most 'safety' flags are measured-and-discarded with respect to the subject's live treatment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: concerns["safety_concern_rate"] = len(safety_issues) / len(trials)  # safety flags only aggregated for reporting

spec_features.spec_quote: Framework makes clear that models aren't sentient
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose at DESIGN.md:1072 ('Framework makes clear that models aren't sentient'). grep for 'sentien|suffer|pattern match|aren't' across all .py files returns nothing. No prompt, system message, or code conveys this framing; it does not change any execution path.
